description: Validates DNS record configurations for type validity, TTL safety, FQDN correctness, no CNAME-at-apex, TLS host consistency, and operational accountability

rules.description: dns-config-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare a non-empty records array. Every record must have hostname, a valid type, and a target
All hostnames must be valid DNS labels. FQDN format is enforced for absolute hostnames (trailing dot). Labels cannot start or end with hyphens
No two records may share the same hostname and type combination within the same zone. Duplicate A/CNAME records for the same name produce undefined resolution behaviour
When spec.tls is declared, every TLS hostname must match at least one DNS record in spec.records. A TLS certificate for a hostname with no DNS record will never be served

TTL values must be integers within the allowed range. Defaults: min=60s (prevents excessive DNS traffic), max=86400s (24h — ensures changes propagate within a day). Range is configurable via spec.ttlPolicy.min/max
rules.note: Skipped for records with no TTL declared; those records are flagged by contract-dns-config (DNS008)

rules.description: CNAME targets must not point to themselves (infinite loop). CNAME targets that are also declared as A records in the same spec are validated for consistency
rules.note: Skipped when no CNAME records are present

rules.description: dns-config-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers

environment must be declared (dns records must be scoped to staging/production). owner must be declared for DNS change accountability. All records should declare explicit TTL — provider defaults are non-deterministic across environments
rules.advisory: Records without explicit TTL are flagged but do not fail the gate
